evidence.requirements: Almost everything is met. The start page lists the title, date and time, price and "<n> seats left" (views.js:58-81, start.jpg). Each tasting has a "Book <title>" link (views.js:70). The form has the labels Name, Email and Guests, 1 to 8, and a "Book" button (views.js:116-128). Seat limits are enforced (booking-rules.js:41-44, bookings.js:62-65). The confirmation shows the heading, tasting, guests, total and reference (views.js:137-156, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and a Sign in button, and the password comes from STAFF_PASSWORD (server.js:19, views.js:159-172). Bookings are grouped by tasting with name, email, guests, reference and a Cancel button, and cancelling frees seats (bookings.js:85-99, staff.jpg). PORT defaults to 3000, storage is in memory and the UI is in English. Two requirements are only partly met. (1) In form.jpg, after an invalid email there is no visible error message next to the form. The `required`/`type=email` attributes (views.js:122) let the browser block the submit and show only a fading native tooltip, so the server-side field errors (views.js:83-86, 98-100) never appear. (2) The seat count says "1 seat left" (format.js:21) instead of the briefed "<n> seats left" format.
evidence.correctness: Seat checks run synchronously in the single-threaded store, so the check and the insert cannot interleave (bookings.js:17-19, 60-77). The store checks seats again as a safety net. The guest count is validated as a whole number with a strict regex: '2.5', '1e1', '-1', '' and '9' are rejected (booking-rules.js:9, 37-46; booking-rules.test.js:43-49). Arrays and non-string fields are treated as empty (booking-rules.js:21-23). The fully booked and "Only N seats left" cases are handled. Cancelling deletes the booking, which frees its seats, and its confirmation URL then returns 404 (app.test.js:335-361). Unknown tastings, unknown references and unknown pages return 404. Body-parser errors are routed to an error page (app.js:160-172). Prices are stored in cents (tastings.js). PORT is validated (server.js:8-15). I found no logic errors.
evidence.security: All dynamic output passes through escapeHtml, including attribute values (views.js:6-17), and a test covers this (app.test.js:225-247). The password check hashes both sides with SHA-256 and compares them with timingSafeEqual (staff-auth.js:41-52). Sessions use 32-byte random tokens kept in memory, expire after 8 hours, and use an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to /staff, with Secure in production (staff-auth.js:55-85). Cancelling requires a per-session CSRF token compared in constant time (app.js:43-48, 144-150). Sign-in is rate-limited (app.js:57-67). Staff pages send no-store. Other measures: a strict CSP and other security headers (app.js:18-35), a 10kb body limit, x-powered-by disabled, booking references from crypto.randomInt, and no secrets in the code. If no password is set, staff sign-in is disabled with a 503 rather than open. There is no sign-out, and the README documents this.
evidence.code_quality: Responsibilities are cleanly separated: tastings, store, validation, auth, views, formatting and app wiring each have their own module, and each is small. Names are clear. Factories (createApp, createBookingStore, createStaffAuth) allow injection for tests. Errors are handled, including a 500 page that hides details. Comments are sparse and explain why something is done (bookings.js:17-19, staff-auth.js:41). The template-string views are readable, and escaping is applied consistently. The size fits the task, with no needless abstraction.
evidence.tests: There are three test files using node:test with no extra dependencies. app.test.js runs about 24 HTTP-level tests that cover every brief requirement: listing and seats left, the booking link and form labels, the confirmation contents, total price, invalid input, the seat limit, fully booked, staff login and wrong password, grouped staff listing, cancel freeing seats, CSRF, forged cookie, rate limit, escaping and the cookie flags. The unit tests cover boundaries (1 and 8, 0 seats, singular wording, non-string input) and store behaviour (unique references, cancel, grouping order). The assertions are specific and check state, not only the responses.
evidence.ux_design: The screenshots show a clean, warm wine-coloured theme with serif headings and card layouts that suit a winery (start.jpg). Dates are readable ("6 November 2026, 18:00"), and the confirmation has a clear summary and a monospace reference (confirmation.jpg). The form keeps entered values and shows a summary of the tasting. Weaknesses: (1) form.jpg shows no persistent error after an invalid email, only a faint, fading native tooltip, so guests get weak feedback. (2) On the staff page the tasting cards touch each other with no gap between them (staff.jpg; styles.css gives .tasting-bookings no margin). (3) Cancel has no confirmation step and there is no sign-out (README:69-70).
evidence.accessibility: The page sets lang="en". Every input has a <label for> (views.js:117-126). On errors, aria-invalid and aria-describedby point to the field error, and a role="alert" summary is shown (views.js:98-101). The focus outline is visible (styles.css:126-130 and form.jpg). Tables use th scope="col" and a visually hidden "Actions" header (views.js:202-206). Sections are labelled by their headings, and dates use <time>. Contrast looks adequate: white on #6b1e2e, and #6d625b on white is about 6:1. Gaps: all Cancel buttons share the same accessible name, with no booking or guest context, and focus is not moved to the error summary.
evidence.simplicity: The app has two runtime dependencies (express, express-rate-limit) and about 600 lines of source, which suits a small booking app. The CSP, security headers, rate limiter and PORT validation go somewhat beyond the brief but are cheap and justified. There is no build step, database or framework bloat.

unmet_requirements: Partly met: "Invalid input is rejected with an error message next to the form". In form.jpg, native type=email/required validation blocks the submit, so no visible error message is shown next to the form, only a transient browser tooltip.
Partly met: seats left is shown as "1 seat left" when one seat remains (format.js:21), instead of the briefed "<n> seats left" format.
strengths: Correct seat accounting with synchronous check-and-insert, a second check in the store, and strict validation of the guest count including boundaries (booking-rules.js, bookings.js)

Strong staff security: constant-time password check, random server-side sessions, an HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to /staff, CSRF tokens on cancel, rate-limited login, CSP, and output escaped everywhere
Thorough, meaningful tests (HTTP and unit) that map directly to each brief requirement and to edge cases
issues: An invalid email shows no persistent error message next to the form (form.jpg): the browser's native validation blocks the submit and the server-side field errors never appear, so feedback is weak
No confirmation step before Cancel and no staff sign-out; all Cancel buttons have the same accessible name with no booking context
Minor visual and wording issues: the staff tasting cards have no spacing between them (staff.jpg), and "1 seat left" departs from the briefed "<n> seats left" format
review.verdict: This is a well-structured, secure and well-tested app that implements the brief almost exactly and looks right for a family winery. It is close to shippable. The main gap is that the browser's native validation hides the app's own error messages for an invalid email, and the staff page needs small fixes: a cancel confirmation, sign-out and spacing between the cards.
